newsitem.title: UK: US funds warm to Japan, split on US - survey.
newsitem.headline: US funds warm to Japan, split on US - survey.

text.p: US fund managers are reversing their low opinion of Japanese equities, with many intending to raise exposure, but sentiment about the domestic market is evenly split, a poll by Merrill Lynch shows.
A balance of 12 percent of respondents, up from four percent in last month's survey, are looking to buy Japanese equities.
The poll was conducted by Gallup between November 29 and December 4, covering 49 institutions responsible for funds totalling $1.90 trillion.
Some 31 percent expect the US economy to improve over the coming year, while 35 percent expect it to get a little worse.
"This division is also visible in their expectations on the Fed funds rate," the survey note said -- 31 percent expect it to be higher in a year's time but the same number expect it to be lower.
Within sectors, enthusiasm has dimmed for financials with a balance of bulls minus bears at 15 percent from 23 percent last month. But it is still favourite, with technology also liked.

Outside the US, Continental Europe is still the favoured destination, with buyers matching sellers of the UK. Asia is attracting some buyers, as is Latin America but many funds are also raising cash weightings, the poll showed.
The dollar is the preferred currency over the next 12 months, followed by sterling, the yen and mark.
